page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is an accelerator-focused instance configured for high-throughput computing and machine learning. Built on KVM virtualization, it provides 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, supporting vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory totals 192 GB of RAM (12 GB per core), paired with three NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering an aggregate 144 GB of VRAM. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and features no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for operating system and data requirements.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across single-core and GPU acceleration tasks. The platform achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2,922 and multi-core score of 20,598, both ranking in the top tier (top 10%), supplemented by top-tier stress-ng single-core performance (4,184.96) and strong multi-core throughput (66,959.75). Large-block memory write bandwidth reaches 203.06 GB/sec (top 10%), while cached read speeds exceed 3,766 GB/sec. For machine learning, the three L40S accelerators deliver top-tier LLM inference performance, processing 6,015 tokens per second for prompt intake and 129.4 tokens per second for text generation on medium 7B models.

Resource allocation presents distinct operational tradeoffs. The 12 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio comfortably accommodates extensive in-memory working sets alongside multi-GPU orchestration. However, the shared CPU allocation and absence of bundled local NVMe storage mean that intensive disk I/O requires network storage, which must be planned around network limits. The instance provides strong compute-to-cost efficiency for multi-GPU inference, parallel data transformation, and neural model serving without the hardware overhead of eight-GPU configurations.

This server type is suited for large-scale language model inference, AI batch processing, computer vision pipelines, image processing, and distributed machine learning tasks requiring high GPU VRAM capacity.
